headline: A 2014 law lets two Texas water agencies move water from Lake Texoma across state lines without violating federal invasive species transfer bans, under specific conditions.
what_it_does: The law creates an exception to federal rules that normally bar moving invasive species across state borders. It covers water transfers by the North Texas Municipal Water District and the Greater Texoma Utility Authority. The exception applies only if the water moves through closed systems drawn from Lake Texoma and any invasive species are removed or killed at treatment facilities.

who_it_affects.how: It can transfer water under the exception if it uses only closed systems from Lake Texoma and removes or eliminates invasive species at its treatment facilities.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on June 9, 2014.
